evidence: Halleck calls Grant a good general, while criticizing care of his command.
limit: [I] Above is role-bounded and qualified; no army-level high or organising gift. Private conversation reported by another participant.

evidence: Halleck explicitly calls Grant brave in battle.
limit: [I] A third-party contemporary leg, not Grant praising himself. No permille conversion.

evidence: The same appraisal calls Grant careless of his command.
limit: No positive organising leg; a single adverse comment does not prove a permanent negative trait.

evidence: Halleck describes Buell as slow but safe.
limit: [I] Operational pace, not deficient courage. Preserve safe rather than treating slowness as general incompetence.

evidence: Halleck describes Buell as slow but safe.
limit: An audience-specific mixed appraisal; not a national reputation measurement.

evidence: Morton calls Buell unfit for the great army, slow and opposed to the proclamation.
limit: Morton was seeking soldier furloughs for the impending Indiana election. Do not turn his political objection into a finding about Buell’s actual policy or innate ability.

evidence: Chase credits Halleck’s intelligence and evident mastery of the business he has taken in hand.
limit: [I] Administrative/general-in-chief role, not field-command genius. Chase disagrees about retaining Buell and McClellan.

evidence: Chase describes evident mastery of the business after observing Halleck explain deployment and a promotion-screening board.
limit: [I] An actual observer appraisal, not inference from the assignment alone; promise and limited observation qualify it. Later counterevidence remains below.

observer: General Hunter, recorded by Chase; given name unresolved
evidence: The speaker acknowledges ability and knowledge but criticizes Halleck’s study and exploitation of situations.
limit: Identity not silently expanded; adverse effort appraisal coexists with ability. This does not independently establish below competence.

evidence: Lincoln says McClellan could put the troops into Washington’s fortifications better than any other man.
limit: [I] Explicit comparative ability appraisal supports a narrow organising observation. It is stronger than the bare assignment, but does not establish field competence or erase contrary views.

observer: Bates, Smith, Welles and Blair, recorded by Chase
evidence: The cabinet discussion criticizes entrusting him with chief command; Lincoln simultaneously trusts his defensive organisation.
limit: Opposed audiences and roles. Preserve the assessments rather than average them into a national centre.

evidence: Chase explicitly withdraws professional confidence and argues against the command.
limit: Political/cabinet observer with a declared history of disagreement; not an adjudication of the allegations.

evidence: Cochrane reports McClellan’s appreciation of Chase’s support and willingness to cooperate.
limit: A mediated reconciliation overture does not establish truthful reporting or resolve their policy differences.

evidence: Chase proposes Burnside, Hooker or Sumner as better alternatives to McClellan.
limit: Preference for appointment is expectation, not demonstrated gift or broad public reputation.

evidence: Stanton thinks Burnside too partial to McClellan to be safe.
limit: [I] Third-party attribution of allegiance, not Burnside’s own declaration or a finding of disloyalty. Entry continues 19 August from p61.

evidence: Chase proposes him for command without a specific account of professional performance.
limit: Assignment preference does not clear this held gift; no December Fredericksburg admission is backdated.

evidence: Pope expresses strong indignation against McClellan and Porter and attributes his failure to them.
limit: [I] Direction of professional antagonism only. Accusations are not adjudicated facts; no permanent shifts_blame trait.

evidence: Pope expresses strong indignation against Porter and seeks publication of his report.
limit: [I] Preserve the interested speaker and occasion; not a verdict on Porter’s conduct.

observer: I. C. H. Smith, recorded by Chase
evidence: Smith eulogizes Pope and McDowell in strong terms.
limit: Specific favorable staff voice is retained; does not measure national standing after defeat.

observer: General Hunter, recorded by Chase; given name unresolved
evidence: The speaker acknowledges energy and ability while denying steady power.
limit: One resentful observer admits having met Stanton only once. Retain the assessment; insufficient foundation for a general centre.

observer: General Hunter, recorded by Chase; given name unresolved
evidence: The speaker accuses Stanton of insincerity.
limit: He admits little acquaintance and relies on unnamed information. Do not convert hostile hearsay into a truthful narrator verdict.

evidence: Stanton answers that nothing has been done about the Mississippi expedition; discussion clarifies that organising orders had issued but little had yet happened.
limit: Difference between an order and execution, not proof of an organising gift or intentional deception.

evidence: Morton seeks furloughs for Indiana regiments to vote and criticizes Buell.
limit: An election request is not enough to replace a held Union-value cell. S6’s separately sourced union observation is preserved.

evidence: He presses Chase to accompany him to Lincoln about the furloughs.
limit: Routine advocacy does not establish a strong temperament band.

evidence: He candidly predicts likely defeat in Indiana and loss of most congressional districts.
limit: [I] Specific adverse disclosure to an ally, not forecast accuracy or comprehensive truthfulness; the election outcome belongs to S3.
